tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

sfg-ppln-implementation: Introduction, p.1: the Letter states its own SFG-in-PPLN implementation and SLM-prepared pump and signal.
scope-nondiffraction-regime: Introduction, p.1: 'At present, we focus on the SF generation in the non-diffraction regime'; diffraction left to future studies.
model-undepleted-pump-qpm: Text after Eq. 3-4, pp.1-2: nondepletion pump approximation 'which is the case in this study'; Eq. 4 valid without strong diffraction. Scope of the paper's own model.
setup-lasers-pulses: Experimental setup, p.2 and Fig. 1 caption: lasers, linewidth, 200 ps and 10 MHz pulses, 13 nm difference stated by the authors.
setup-powers: Experimental setup, p.2: average and peak powers for pump and signal after two EDFAs.
setup-crystal-and-focusing: Experimental setup, p.2: PPLN dimensions, 19.36 um period, f=200 mm, 775.75 nm SF, waists 45 and 41 um.
setup-slm-phase-masks: Experimental setup, p.2: Santec SLM-100, 1 cm x 1 cm area, 10.4 um pitch, incidence angles 50 and 55 degrees.
setup-detection: Experimental setup, p.2: two short-pass filters, power meter or Canon Rebel T5 CCD with stated sensor and pitch.
low-conversion-regime: Experimental setup, p.2: authors state measurements are in the low conversion regime, restricted by laser power and 2 mm crystal.
definition-eta-xi: Experimental setup, p.2: eta and xi defined in the text exactly as the value says.
pso-pump-optimization: Optimization section, p.3: PSO method and particle definition as stated; the paper's own method.
feedback-algorithm-steps: Fig. 3 caption, p.3: eight steps listed and match the value.
funding-onr: Acknowledgments, p.4: the paper states its own ONR award number. No basis fits exactly; this is a statement about the paper itself, so setup is the nearest. Coordinator may override.
system-eom-fpga-hybrid: Section 1, p.2 and Section 3: the paper builds an EOM plus FPGA RC system. 'Fully-packaged' is the authors' wording.
time-delay-rc-virtual-nodes: Section 2, p.3: text defines the time-delay RC with virtual nodes, one nonlinear node, EOM nonlinearity.
eom-nonlinear-transfer-function: Section 2, Eqs. 3-9, p.4: sin^2 transfer function in RF drive, V_pi and bias, detector, filter and delay, discretized state Eq. 9; read in the text layer.
hardware-optical-and-adc-dac: Section 3, p.4: ~1550 nm CW laser diode, EOM, ADC 1 Msps, 16-bit MAX11198 ADC and D5541A DAC over SPI.
fpga-platform-zedboard-verilog: Section 3, p.4: Zedboard Zynq-7000, Verilog, PC to Zedboard over Ethernet, PS returns state data to PC.
fpga-delay-1000-filter-400-taps: Section 3, p.5: delay limited to 1000 units, 400-tap bandpass filter.
gain-offset-key-tuning-parameters: Section 3, p.5: gain and offset stated as key tuning parameters; calibration DAC compensates EOM bias drift.
narma10-task-setup: Section 4.1, p.5: input uniform on [0,0.5]; NRMSE defined with target standard deviation (Eq. 11).
santafe-task-setup: Section 4.2, p.6: data set A, NH3 laser, one-step prediction, 4000 points, NMSE.
spoken-digit-data-and-preprocessing: Section 4.3, p.7: AudioMNIST, 30,000 samples, 60 speakers, 48 kHz, librosa to 12 kHz, zero padding to 12,000, Lyon cochleagram.
spoken-digit-split-protocol: Section 4.3, p.7: 20 balanced subsets of 100 samples, 4 train and 1 test, 50 random datasets for WER.
spoken-digit-mask-readout: Section 4.3 and Fig. 6 caption, p.7: mask uniform in [-1,1], 77 channels, serial injection, argmax of row-wise mean.
limitation-low-speed-adc-dac: Section 5, p.9: the authors state low speed limited by ADC sampling rate and DAC settling time.
partial-fourier-approach: Introduction, p.1: the paper studies partial Fourier transform by displacing the crystal from the Fourier-lens focus.
previous-system-limitation: Introduction, p.1: the authors state that their own earlier system [30] overlooks original-domain features; Fig. 2 (81.25% to 99.23%) supports it. Limit of the authors' prior work, stated by them.
setup-hardware: Experimental setup, p.2: f=200 mm Fourier lens, temperature-stabilized PPLN, SF power readings feed a DNN.
setup-simulation-method: Experimental setup, p.2: split-step Fourier and adaptive step size solve Eqs. 1-3; period 19.36 um. Text says 'can use', and Fig. 2 states these are simulated results, so read as the method.
setup-dataset: Dataset paragraph, p.3: first 200 MNIST images per digit, 1600/400 split, 28x28 raised to 400x400.
setup-network: Network paragraph, p.3: one conv plus five FC layers (as in [30]), ADAM, softmax.
setup-lg-modes-and-delta: Results, p.3: 40 LG modes following [30]; delta 0, 27, 40 mm chosen given the defocus trade-off; stated by the authors.
noise-snr-definition: Eq. 4, p.4: SNR defined as 10 log10 of the phase-value variance ratio.
previous-normalization-fragility: Results, pp.2-3: authors state the earlier per-mode normalization is prone to noise and needs renormalizing when data are added. Limit of their own earlier method.
lg-hg-limit: Results, p.4: 'in practice the optimum mode choice shall depend on the spatial characteristics of the target images', a caveat on the paper's LG over HG comparison (Fig. 5).
kumar2021-model-ignores-space-time-coupl: Section II, p.1: the field is the product of spatial and temporal parts, inter-coupling ignored.
kumar2021-selectivity-definition: Section II, Eqs. 6-7, pp.1-2: normalized SF photons in dB with equal input photons per mode; selectivity as difference. Matches the text.
kumar2021-setup-source-and-wavelengths: Section III, p.3: mode-locked laser 0.3 ps at 50 MHz, two 100 GHz WDMs, pump 1545 nm and signal 1558 nm.
kumar2021-setup-pump-signal-power: Section III, p.3: EDFA, ~10 mW maximum average pump on the crystal; signal attenuated with ND filters.
kumar2021-setup-slm-beams: Section III, p.3: FWHM 2.8 and 2.6 mm, Santec SLM-100 1440x1050 at 10.4 um, F=200 mm.
kumar2021-setup-ppln-efficiency: Section III, p.3: PPLN 19.36 um, 10 mm x 3 mm x 1 mm; normalized efficiency 1% stated as a crystal parameter.
kumar2021-setup-detection-filtering: Section III, pp.3-4: short-pass and bandpass filters with >180 dB total extinction; Si-APD ID100 at 15%; Zedboard FPGA readout.
kumar2021-setup-optimizer: Section III, p.4: MATLAB random-walk adaptive feedback; FPGA collects counts, sends to computer.
kumar2021-optimized-pump-composition: Section IV, p.3: pump superposition of 18 LG modes, l in [-5:5], p in [0,1], as quoted. The 18-mode count is below the 22 index combinations, so it is a subset, but the value says only what the text says.
kumar2021-temporal-shaping-by-delay-only: Discussion, Section V, p.5: spatial shaping by SLM, temporal shaping only by time delay; an OAWG is proposed for future work, attributed as a proposal.
setup-laser-pump: Experimental setup, p.1: 1550.9 nm mode-locked laser, 70 mW, 3.8 mm FWHM on the SLM.
setup-slm-lattice: Experimental setup, p.1: Santec SLM-100, 10 um pixels, 20x20 giant spins of 20x20 pixels.
setup-ppln-optics: Experimental setup, pp.1-2: F=200 mm lens, PPLN 19.36 um, 1 cm, SH near 775.5 nm.
setup-feedback-loop-boltzmann: Experimental setup, p.2: MATLAB feedback loop updating the SLM; Boltzmann acceptance P=exp(-dU/T).
def-spin-encoding: Experimental setup p.1 and Theoretical Model p.2: phase 0 or pi, sigma_i = +/-1 is the pump phase.
model-nondiffraction-nondepletion: Theoretical Model, p.2: model stated for the pump non-diffraction and non-depletion regime.
def-hamiltonian: Theoretical Model, Eq. 4, p.2: Hamiltonian defined as the superposition of pump and SH intensities, with the -1 on pump and gamma; two-body and four-body terms.
limit-low-rank-interactions: Theoretical Model, p.3: authors state the low-rank interactions 'may impose some limitations' on the SLM-based machine; they also list ways around it.
limit-simulation-optical-loss: Experimental results, p.3: authors state optical loss is not captured in their model and is one mechanism for the simulation-experiment discrepancy.
setup-mean-field-assumptions: Mean-field theory, p.3: MF theory assumes uniform two-body and four-body constants and small magnetization fluctuation.
setup-uniform-constants-fig3: Fig. 3 caption, p.4: uniform interactions with J~0.19 uW and K~3.6e-9 uW used in panels (b,c).
scope-optimization-efficiency-untested: Introduction, p.1: the work is 'the first step' and investigates ground-state magnetic phases; the paper shows no optimization benchmark (checked against the full text).

theory_low.kumar2021-sim-s4-selectivity: A single simulated example (Fig. 2) with random-walk optimization, Section II. A numerical outcome, not a proved result.
theory_low.rank-two-body-one-four-body-N: Stated in the text with the decomposition J_ij=P_iP_j; the rank-N claim for Q_ij rests on an informal reason ('fiber mixes light') and the equation line is garbled. Not a stated and proved theorem.
theory_low.result-mf-self-consistent-equation: Mean-field derivation under assumed uniform constants and small fluctuations; Eq. 10 follows from dF/dm=0 by 'a straightforward calculation' with steps not shown. The consistency with Monte-Carlo (Fig. 3b,c) is a numerical comparison. Not a stated and proved theorem.
theory_low.result-gamma-zero-second-order-tc: Landau-type argument from the truncated expansion (Eq. 11, garbled in the text layer); Landau's theory is cited [50], the expansion steps are not shown, Tc=2NJ is an approximate result. Not a proved result.
theory_low.result-gamma-positive-second-order-persi: Qualitative argument from the sign of the quartic coefficient in the truncated expansion (p.5); not stated as a theorem and not proved.
theory_low.result-critical-gamma-c: An approximate critical value from a truncated expansion; the authors say it differs from the numerical value because higher-order terms are ignored. gamma_c~55 is a computed comparison, not a proved result.
theory_low.result-first-order-mechanism-and-boundar: Mean-field reasoning with the boundary 'estimated' from F(m=0)=F(m=1) in a simplified form; the linear-increase conclusion is qualitative and supported by Fig. 3 numerics. Not a proved result.
theory_low.result-gamma-negative-second-order: Reported from the mean-field phase diagram, Fig. 3(c), p.5; a numerical outcome, not a proved result.
